summary: Confirmed that candidate 4f47bef only covers stale/dead advisory-lock owners and leaves the registered MXFP4 test unbounded for live compiler or kernel stalls. Added a process-group-isolated, 120-second-per-attempt supervisor with fresh SGLANG_JIT_CACHE_DIR and TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR and one timeout retry, while retaining the candidate's valid lock regressions.

tests.what_was_measured: The candidate's two advisory-lock recovery regressions passed: 2 passed, 42 deselected.
A live owner held _build_lock beyond the independent deadline; the contender had no internal timeout.
45 passed, including dead-owner recovery and the registered MXFP4 supervisor killing a stalled first process group and succeeding with a second fresh cache.
The actual registered entry used a fresh cache and reached hipcc targeting gfx950, then failed because the NVIDIA-specific source includes unavailable cuda_bf16.h; no kernel executed.

tests.command: pre-commit run ruff --files test/registered/expert_pack/test_expert_pack_mxfp4.py test/registered/kernels/test_jit_cache.py && pre-commit run ruff-format --files test/registered/expert_pack/test_expert_pack_mxfp4.py test/registered/kernels/test_jit_cache.py
tests.what_was_measured: Both changed Python files passed lint and formatting.

gpu_evidence: The assigned gfx950 was selected and hipcc was invoked with --offload-arch=gfx950:sramecc+:xnack-, but compilation stopped at missing cuda_bf16.h before any MXFP4 GPU kernel ran.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA H200 was available, so the intermittent H200 event and MXFP4 numerical behavior were not reproduced.
The available ROCm toolchain cannot compile this NVIDIA-specific source because cuda_bf16.h is absent.

The supervisor regression deterministically validates timeout, process-group termination, fresh-cache retry, and the registered executable path; hardware prevented a passing end-to-end MXFP4 JIT/kernel run.
